name: ducati_1098_testastretta
label: Ducati 1098 Testastretta Evoluzione 1099 cc 90° L-twin
based_on: Ducati Testastretta Evoluzione 1099 cc L-twin, Ducati 1098 / 1098 S, 2007-2008

sources.what: Ducati's own 2008 Superbike technical specification sheet (848, 1098, 1098 S, 1098 R), PDF titled SBK08_TechSpec.xls, hosted by a German motorcycle news site. Manufacturer document.
Ducati's 2008 Superbike press kit text (same host). Manufacturer document: valve diameters, throttle bodies, exhaust layout and tube diameters.
Ducati 1098 owner's manual, page 101 (engine and performance data), as transcribed by a manuals site. Manufacturer document; read through a page summary, so quotes are as the summary returned them.
Ducati 1098 owner's manual, page 102 (spark plugs, fuel system, throttle body diameter).
Ducati 1098 Tricolore use and maintenance manual, page 100; cross-check of bore, stroke, compression, 113 kW, 116 Nm and 10,700 rpm. Not used as a primary source.

bikeboy.org (Brad Black, Australian Ducati tuner): table of 998 / 998S / 999R / 1098 cam specs and measured as-delivered timing. Third party, well regarded among Ducati tuners, not a factory document.
Same author's four-valve cam timing article; source for the statement that Ducati cam specs are given at 1.00 mm lift.
ducatiforum.co.uk thread on finding firing TDC on an 848; quotes the workshop manual and gives vertical cylinder firing 270 crank degrees after horizontal. Forum.
ducatiforum.co.uk thread identifying Ducati rods by eye-to-eye length. Forum; only source found for rod length.
Motorcycle Mojo magazine technical column on crankshafts and firing orders; states the 270/450 spacing of a 90-degree V-twin such as a Ducati.
SlashGear explainer on the L-twin; states shared crank pin and 270/450 intervals. General-interest, weak but explicit.

notes: Sourced: bore, stroke, compression ratio, 90-degree L-twin on a shared crank pin, horizontal cylinder firing first and the vertical one 270 degrees later (intervals 270/450; the order is from a forum quoting the workshop manual), rod length 124 mm (forum, weak), four valves per cylinder, valve diameters 42/34 mm, cam timing and lift (a tuner's table of factory figures, presumed at 1 mm lift), 60 mm throttle bodies, 2-1-2 exhaust in 52 and 57 mm tubing, 10,700 rpm maximum speed, published power and torque (Ducati's spec sheet; the owner's manual gives lower figures, 113 kW and 116 Nm). Estimated, not sourced: that the cam table is at 1 mm lift; that 52 mm is the header and 57 mm the later pipe (both taken as given, though they are probably outside diameters); intake length (0.32 m) and diameter (58 mm at the valve end; the model uses the runner's area as the throttle area, so the sourced 60 mm throttle figure is recorded but not used); header length (0.88 m), the single pipe and silencer dimensions; idle speed (1250 rpm); flywheel inertia; friction_scale 0.6, heat_q 2.7e6 and burn_scale 0.7, the first two at the end of their allowed range.

vehicle.name: Ducati 1098 (2007)
vehicle.notes: curb_kg is estimated: the owner's manual's 188 kg 'running order without fuel' plus a full 15.5 L tank. final_drive is primary 59:32 (1.84) x chain 38:15. top_speed_kmh is Cycle World's radar figure (174 mph) for the 1098 S, which has the same engine and gearing and was on the rev limiter in sixth; no figure was found for the base bike. wheel_radius_m is calculated from the tyre size.
